issues.issue: The duty extends to "conducting litigation, arbitration or other proceedings", although the Policy contains no arbitration agreement and Condition 5.10 requires all claims and disputes to be litigated in named New York courts.
The clause is numbered 3.6 although it sits in Section 5 (Conditions) between 5.5 and 5.7, so the internal numbering does not identify it.
It presupposes "all other Insureds" beyond the first listed, which cannot be squared with definition 3.7 defining the Insured as the single entity listed on the Declaration Page.
The clause deducts "the applicable coinsurance", but the Declaration Page states no coinsurance percentage at all, so the second step of the calculation cannot be performed.

It directs that the Self-Insured Retention be "apportioned" as calculated under Condition 5.14, but Condition 5.14 (Self-Insured Retention) contains no apportionment mechanism and simply applies the retention to each and every Loss.
The insured may cancel "by the surrender of this Policy" or on ten days' notice, but the clause does not say when surrender takes effect, and "short rate portion" is left unquantified.

"[A]ll claims and disputes will be litigated in" the named New York courts reads as mandatory and exclusive, but the clause never uses words of exclusivity, so whether it merely consents to those forums is open.

The Service of Suit Endorsement (SL-704 CA) has the insurer agree, at the insured's request, to submit to "a court of competent jurisdiction within the United States" and expressly "applies in California"; it cannot be squared with an exclusive New York forum.

The condition operates on "the Coinsurance amount stated on the Declaration Page", but the Declaration Page states limits, sub-limits and retentions and no coinsurance amount at all, so the mechanism has nothing to work on.
The Policy is "null and void" for any non-disclosure of a material fact "whether or not fraudulent", a strict forfeiture whose reach depends entirely on the undefined test of materiality.

The insured may not disclose the Policy's existence "to any person or party whether within or outside the Insured" except as required to comply with the Policy or by law, which on its face bars disclosure to its own brokers, auditors and counsel.

This condition applies the retention "separately to each and every Loss", while the Declaration Page states each Self-Insured Retention "per Insured Event"; a single Insured Event can generate many Losses under Section 2.

"[D]ue diligence to do all things reasonable and practical to avoid any happening or circumstances covered by this Policy" sets no benchmark, and read literally it obliges the insured to avoid the very events it insured against.

Condition 5.17 permits other insurance only "over the Limit of Liability" and on written notice, while Condition 5.24 permits other insurance "written on the same terms and conditions as this Policy" without any notice requirement.
The final sentence excepts "Crisis Consultant Costs" from the aggregate but still calls all expenses "part of Loss", leaving unclear whether those costs erode the Limit of Liability at all.

Condition 5.19 extends reporting to thirty days after "the expiration of this Policy", whereas the Section 1 insuring clause extends it to thirty days after "non-renewal of the Policy"; the two triggers differ.
The clause assumes "more than one Insured", which conflicts with definition 3.7's single named entity on the Declaration Page.

The sub-paragraphs cross-refer to "notice under (a)" and determinations "under (c)" although the list is numbered (i)-(v), and written notice is due "within 5 days or as soon as is practicable, whichever is earlier", which sets two inconsistent deadlines.
Sub-paragraph (iv) requires compliance with "Condition 8., Statement of Loss", but the Policy has no Condition 8; the statement-of-loss requirements are in Condition 5.28.

Condition 5.23 directs all notices to the address "shown on the Declaration Page", while Condition 5.22 requires loss notifications to be addressed to Starr Adjustment Services in Atlanta, an address not on the Declaration Page.

Condition 5.24 makes this Policy co-insure where a Kidnap and Ransom/Extortion policy exists, while Condition 5.17 states that the existence of other insurance "will not reduce the Insurers' liability under this Policy".

The clause says "The Insurer's right to salvage will not be restricted by the Insured" and in the next breath that the Insured "will have full right to the possession of all goods" and "will retain control of all damaged goods"; the two sentences pull in opposite directions.
"[T]he state wherein this Policy is issued" is not identified: the insurer is in New York, the insured and the delivery are in California, so which state's statutes amend the Policy is left open.

This conformance provision points to the law of the state of issue, while Condition 5.10 fixes New York law and New York forums and the Service of Suit Endorsement states "This applies in California".

"The Insurers shall determine the amount of any Loss" sits against Condition 5.4 Appraisal, which provides that where the parties "fail to agree as to the amount of Loss" appraisers and an umpire determine it.
The list runs "taking into account:- a. the future profitability ... and" then an unlettered paragraph about market changes; the missing "b." leaves the second factor's status uncertain.
"[S]tandard accounting principles as recognized by the relevant regulatory authorities in the Insured's jurisdiction" names no identifiable body of principles or authority.

The window for the final statement of loss (no earlier than 12 and no later than 24 months) interacts with Condition 5.2, which runs the 24-month suit limitation from submission of that final statement, and with the closing words that nothing overrides Condition 5.22.
The insured must demonstrate the probable level of sales "with reasonable certainty", a standard of proof imposed by the policy without any definition of what will satisfy it.

"Words that are specifically not defined in this Policy have the meaning normally attributed to them" is garbled: the intended sense is words not specifically defined, and as written it says the opposite.
Cover depends on the Insured having "a legal obligation to reimburse or pay that customer", a condition that imports an undefined external liability test into the coverage grant.

The endorsement covers a customer's economic loss the Insured must reimburse, which sits against Section 2's requirement that Loss be expenses "incurred by the Insured directly and solely" in connection with an Insured Event.

The replacement 4.5 drops the original's "including, but not limited to" and carves out Customer Loss of Gross Profit, so its interaction with the unamended third-party-claim exclusion printed in Section 4 must be worked out.
The $3,000,000 Customer Loss of Gross Profit limit does not say whether it sits inside or on top of the $3,000,000 Policy Aggregate Limit on the Declaration Page and Condition 5.19.
The added retention is "per Insured Event", while Condition 5.14 applies the Self-Insured Retention separately to each and every Loss.
"[S]atisfactory documentary evidence" is a condition precedent measured by no stated standard and, by implication, satisfactory to the insurer alone.
The endorsement announces that it "modifies" the coverage form without saying which provision it displaces, which matters because Condition 5.10 already fixes an exclusive New York forum.

The endorsement's operative terms are cast in terms of "the Company", while the body of the Policy throughout uses "the Insurer"; whether the endorsement's obligations bind the same party under the Policy's defined vocabulary is left to inference.

"This applies in California" is a four-word limitation whose operative sense — that the endorsement is attached because of California law, or that it operates only as to California proceedings — cannot be fixed from the words.
A California-facing endorsement sits against Condition 5.10, which selects New York law and requires all claims to be litigated in New York courts.

"[A]t your request will submit to the jurisdiction of a court of competent jurisdiction within the United States" leaves open whether the insured may choose any competent court or only consents to personal jurisdiction once a court is otherwise proper.

The submission cannot readily be squared with Condition 5.10, under which the parties "expressly agree that all claims and disputes will be litigated in" the New York Supreme Court or the Southern District of New York.

The reservation preserves rights to remove or "to seek a transfer of a case to another court", which pulls against the submission to the insured's chosen forum in the preceding sentence of the same endorsement.
Whether this reservation leaves Condition 5.10's New York forum clause available to the insurer as a basis for transfer is the very question the two provisions read together do not answer.
The promise to "abide by the final decision of such court" reinforces the insured's forum choice under the endorsement and must be reconciled with Condition 5.10's exclusive New York forum.

"All other terms and conditions of this Policy remain unchanged" leaves Condition 5.10's New York forum clause nominally intact alongside the Service of Suit submission, so the priority between them is unresolved.

The statement that no prior written consent is required for red24 sits against definitions 3.4 and 3.14, which make consultant costs recoverable only for consultants "hired with the Insurer's prior written consent" unless pre-approved.

The list of consultant types includes "Producer Defect", which is not one of the four Insured Events defined in 3.8 (Accidental Contamination, Governmental Recall, Malicious Product Tampering, Insured Product Extortion).
This page states only that notice must be given "in writing as soon as is practible", omitting Condition 5.22's five-day written notice requirement and its status as a condition precedent.
